The core investment question is whether the Business segment can stabilize revenue and demonstrate positive operating leverage after shedding Mass Markets, or whether legacy service erosion (local voice, network access, private line per S26) will continue to outpace growth in PCF and AI-related connectivity products. The company generated $4.7B in operating cash flow in 2025 despite -$1.7B net income, proving cash generation capability, but the $4.4B capex run rate leaves only $371M in free cash flow (3.0% margin), creating minimal cushion if revenue deterioration persists or AI demand disappoints. Operating margin swung to -6.5% in 2025 from positive 3.5% in 2024 (calculated from $460M / $13.1B), partially driven by the $628M non-cash goodwill impairment but also reflecting underlying profitability pressure. Without visibility into post-divestiture Business segment revenue trends, PCF contract pipeline and revenue recognition, and debt paydown strategy, the thesis remains binary: either management successfully pivots to enterprise connectivity growth and the divestiture proceeds buy time to execute, or the company burns through liquidity while revenue erosion continues. The next filing will reveal whether the Business segment stabilized after shedding Mass Markets and how much financial flexibility the divestiture actually created.
